questions.q:
Direction: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

The three of them shouted out to each another when the train started moving.
o: shouted out to each another
questions.s:
The correct answer is 'shouted out to each another'.

Key Points

  • The erroneous Part 'shouted out to each another' will be 'shouted out to 'one another'. 
  • The given sentence is an example of Reciprocal Pronoun. 
  • We know that 'each other' is used when there are two people.
    • Example: Bill and Ted are being excellent to each other. 
    • This means Bill is being excellent to Ted, and Ted is being excellent to Bill. They’re practicing what you might call excellence reciprocity.
  • We know that when we are talking about more than two people, we should use a different reciprocal pronoun that is 'one another'. 
    • Example: People need to know one another to be at their honest best.
  • In the given sentence 'The three' is the subject and with them, we should use 'one another'. 
    ​

Thus the correct sentence is: The three of them shouted out to one another when the train started moving. 

Additional Information

  • In the given sentence 'Shout out to' is a phrasal verb. Its meaning is as follows: 
    • Shout out to: When you give a shout-out to someone, it's usually to express appreciation or thanks—or just to recognize their presence. Shout-out often refers to a name check, meaning it specifically names a person 
      • Example: I'd like to give a quick shout out to Debbie, whose birthday is today!

o: Payal as well as her friends
questions.s:

questions.s:

questions.q:
Which type of pronoun is the underlined word?

The boy who came here is her son.
questions.s:
The correct answer is option 3), i.e. Relative pronoun.

Explanation:

The underlined word 'who' has introduced a relative clause, so, it is a relative pronoun.

A pronoun is a word that is used instead of a noun and it functions like a noun. Example: She is your teacher.
There are 10 types of pronouns.

Let's see the function and examples of those pronouns:

Types Function Example
Personal pronoun refers to three persons,i.e. first person,second person and third person I,you,she/he        
Possessive pronoun     to show ownership The bag is mine.
Demonstrative pronoun     to mention something in a sentence specifically This is her pen.
Distributive pronoun        separates the members of a group Each student of the class.  
Reciprocal pronoun         to express reciprocal relationship They hate each other.                     
Reflexive pronoun           The words end with 'self' are called reflexive pronoun and used to show that the subject and the object are same. She is preparing a cake for herself.
Emphatic pronoun             To emphasize the noun or pronoun

She herself can solve the problem.
Indefinite pronoun           to denote indefinite persons or objects Somebody has taken my watch.
Relative pronoun             to introduce relative clauses This is the cake which my mother has prepared.
Interrogative pronoun      asks questions Who is she?


So, 'who' is a 'relative pronoun'.

Relative clauses are clauses starting with the relative pronouns who, that, which, whose, where, when. They are most often used to define or identify the noun that precedes them.

questions.q: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: before we stepped out
to wear snow boots
there was a good idea
questions.s:
Explanation:

  • The segment “there was a good idea” is grammatically incorrect in this context.

  • You don't say “there was a good idea to...” — the correct structure is:

"It was a good idea to..."

So the sentence should be:

We thought it was a good idea to wear snow boots before we stepped out.

🛠️ Part of Speech with Error:

Pronoun/Structure Error — incorrect usage of “there was” instead of “it was.”

🗒️ Hindi Explanation:

यह कहना कि "there was a good idea..." गलत है। सही रूप होगा —
👉 "हमें लगा कि यह एक अच्छा विचार था..." → "We thought it was a good idea..."

✅ Correct Sentence:

We thought it was a good idea to wear snow boots before we stepped out.

✔️ Final Answer: there was a good idea ✅
